A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 Appendix A reports original synthetic-MDP simulations, including corruption, reward-variance, reward-agnostic parameter, and Markovian-sampling experiments.

after.justification: V2 Appendix G reports original synthetic-MDP simulations and experiments on FrozenLake, CliffWalking, and Taxi.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects quantile indices from ζM and (1−ζ)M to ζM/2 and (1−ζ)M/2. The known-reward threshold replaces its uncertainty multiplier with the noise bound σ̄. Appendix F also replaces the original Markovian threshold with Eq. (110), incorporating subsampling into the burn-in and concentration term. These refine the existing filtering-and-thresholding procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates synthetic grid-world MDPs only. V2 adds FrozenLake-v1, CliffWalking-v1, and Taxi-v3, including goal-specific and cliff-specific reward corruption. Explicit Student-t noise and time-growing attacks further broaden the evaluated input conditions.

E2.justification: Vanilla-Q remains the external comparison method. The additional environments reuse this comparator; neither version evaluates another external robust-RL baseline.

E3.justification: The initial synthetic setup changes from 25 states, 4 actions, and discount 0.5 to 25 states, 10 actions, and discount 0.7; additional larger MDP configurations are introduced. New experiments add episodic training, policy-value error, episode-length measurements, and clean greedy-policy evaluation. CliffWalking and Taxi evaluate 200 clean episodes every 400 and 100 training episodes, respectively.

E4.justification: V2 adds a corruption-free Student-t comparison to isolate heavy-tail robustness, plus variance sensitivity under stronger fixed and time-growing attacks. Clean-policy checks under goal suppression and cliff-reward reversal test whether corrupted training returns conceal behavioral failure. The existing reward-agnostic parameter sensitivity analysis is retained and reworked.

E5.justification: V1 generally reports averages over 50 runs, with 100 for the reward-agnostic experiment. V2 reports 100 runs throughout and explicitly identifies an individual-run envelope in Figure 11. Because experimental settings also change, these counts do not establish additional runs of identical experiments.

E6.justification: V2 replaces synthetic results under revised settings and adds numerous findings, including heavy-tail stability and near-clean evaluation returns for robust variants on CliffWalking and Taxi. V1's exact steady-state error figures and standalone RAQ-M plot are absent. These are not matched-setting performance gains. The new FrozenLake Figure 7 also has an unexplained inconsistency between its error scale and stated clean-policy metric.

T1.justification: V2 sharpens the corruption terms from max(R̄, σ̄) to σ̄, changes Theorem 3's probability lower bound from 1/2 to 1/4, and replaces its final argument with a Bretagnolle–Huber argument. It corrects martingale constants and weights and adds a derivation of sufficient ergodicity conditions. The separate known-statistics Markov bound is omitted, while the principal rate orders and assumptions remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: robust asynchronous Q-learning, reward-agnostic operation, near-optimal finite-time guarantees, an unavoidable corruption-dependent error, and extension to Markovian data. The added evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of goal and cliff reward poisoning and why corrupted training returns can misrepresent policy quality. It removes v1's explicit discussion of the unresolved visitation-probability dependence, stronger adversarial timing control, and growing computational and memory costs. Existing qualifications about required parameter knowledge remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly identifies C approximately equal to 100 as the experimental threshold constant and expands practical parameter guidance. However, v1's synthetic-experiment step sizes, 0.1 and 0.001/t, and approximate mixing time of 10 are no longer disclosed. The reported hardware is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Durrett, Lattimore and Szepesvári, and the Gymnasium paper, while removing several application and future-direction references. The substantive positioning against earlier robust Q-learning and TD-learning work is retained in Appendix A.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the lower bound joins the main-results section, Markovian sampling becomes a subsection, prior-work comparisons and practical remarks move to Appendix A, and experiments move to the final appendix. The abstract is rewritten, remarks are consolidated, and the extensive future-directions section becomes a short conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, removes the standalone title-page and contents arrangement, and changes theorem and algorithm presentation. The experimental displays expand from four figures to eleven, with regrouped panels, logarithmic axes, and added shaded variability displays.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects quantile indexing, sharpens theoretical bounds, and adds useful behavioral evaluations beyond toy MDPs. However, Figure 7 reports clean FrozenLake policy-value errors above 10^4 despite describing a task with a single terminal reward of 1, leaving the reported metric unresolved. Explicit qualifications about visitation-probability dependence and some reproducibility details also disappear. These benefits and reporting concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the PDFs alone.
